Course Name: Introduction to Application of Artificial Intelligence to Robotics
                             Instructor: Prof. Pushparaj Mani Pathak

                 WEEK 4: ASSIGNMENT 4

   Q.1   Which polynomial trajectory is commonly used to achieve (C2) continuity in joint-
          space trajectory planning?

         (A) Linear

          (B) Quadratic

          (C) Cubic

         (D) Quintic

          Explanation: (D) Refer slide 21 in Lecture Joint-Space Scheme

          Solving 6 coefficients with 6 boundary conditions maintains C2 continuity


   Q.2  Why  is a cubic polynomial commonly selected for  rest-to-rest  joint  trajectory
          generation?

         (A) It minimizes computation time.

          (B) It satisfies exactly four boundary conditions.

          (C) It guarantees C² continuity.

         (D) It eliminates inverse kinematics.

          Explanation: (B) Refer slide 11 in Lecture Joint-Space Scheme

      A cubic polynomial has four coefficients, allowing  it to satisfy four boundary
           conditions: initial/final positions and initial/final velocities.


   Q.3   Which trajectory structure is commonly used to ensure continuity of velocity and
           acceleration?

         (A) Cubic splines with exponential blends

          (B) Linear splines with parabolic blends

          (C) Circular splines with quintic interpolation

         (D) Polynomial splines without blending

          Explanation: (B) Refer Slide 6 of Lecture Cartesian Space Schemes

         Because they provide smooth velocity and acceleration profiles.





                                                                                   1 | P a g e

optionExplanations.o1: A quadratic supplies only three coefficients.

Q.4  Why must the angle–axis representation be carefully selected before interpolating
      between two orientations?

      (A) Because the angle–axis representation is undefined for rotations above 180°.

      (B) Because  it  is  not  unique, and  the  representation with minimum angular
       displacement should be chosen.

      (C) Because Euler angles are more accurate.

      (D) Because inverse kinematics requires unique joint angles.

       Explanation: (B) Refer Slide 8 of Lecture Cartesian Space Schemes

      The same orientation can be represented by adding multiples of 360°. Therefore, the
       representation minimizing ∣𝐾𝐵−𝐾𝐴∣is selected to ensure the smallest rotational
       displacement during interpolation.


Q.5   Which statement correctly distinguishes repeatability from accuracy?

      (A) Repeatability refers to reaching mathematically defined points.

      (B) Accuracy refers to returning to a previously taught point.

      (C) Repeatability  is returning to a taught point, while accuracy  is reaching a
       mathematically defined point.

      (D) Both terms have identical meanings.

       Explanation: (C) Refer Slide 11 of Lecture Manipulator Mechanism Design-I

       Repeatability measures how consistently a robot returns to a taught position, whereas
      accuracy measures closeness to a mathematically specified position.


Q.6   For the planar 2-DOF articulated manipulator  (𝑙1 = 5,  𝑙2 = 4), which statement
       correctly describes its reachable workspace?

      (A) Circular region with radius 9

      (B) Rectangular region bounded by ±9 units

      (C) Annular region satisfying 1 ≤𝑅≤9

      (D) Cylindrical workspace

       Explanation: (C) Refer Slide 29 of Lecture Manipulator Mechanism Design-I

      Combining the forward kinematics with the link lengths gives a maximum reach of 9
      and a minimum reach of ∣5 −4 ∣= 1. Therefore, all reachable end-effector positions
         lie within an annular region satisfying 1 ≤𝑅≤9.





                                                                               2 | P a g e

Q.7   Which characteristic of a 7-DOF manipulator primarily enables effective collision
      avoidance?

      (A) Reduced actuator torque requirement

      (B) Multiple joint configurations for a given end-effector pose

      (C) Elimination of inverse kinematics

      (D) Increased workspace compared with every serial manipulator

       Explanation: (B) Refer Slide 3 of Lecture Manipulator Mechanism Design-II

      Unlike a 6-DOF robot, which has only a finite number of solutions for a pose, a 7-
    DOF manipulator offers  infinitely many solutions. This redundancy allows the
       controller to select configurations that avoid obstacles.


Q.8  Why can compliant links or transmission systems degrade positioning accuracy in
        industrial manipulators?

      (A) Joint sensors stop functioning.

      (B) Tool position is directly measured incorrectly.

      (C) Forward kinematics assumes rigid components, while compliant components sag
      under load.

      (D) The manipulator loses degrees of freedom.

       Explanation: (C) Refer Slide 12 of Lecture Manipulator Mechanism Design-II

       Industrial manipulators estimate tool position using forward kinematics based on
      sensed joint positions rather than direct tool sensing. Compliance causes sag under
       gravity or loading, producing positioning errors despite accurate joint sensing.


Q.9   The primary reason a SCARA robot is described as selectively compliant is that it is:

      (A) Flexible in the Z-direction and rigid in the X–Y plane

      (B) Rigid in the X–Y plane and compliant in all rotational axes

      (C) Rigid in the Z-direction while compliant in the X–Y plane

      (D) Equally compliant in all directions

       Explanation: (C) Refer Slide 4 of Lecture Manipulator Design Example

    A SCARA manipulator is designed to be rigid along the vertical (Z) axis while
       allowing limited compliance in the horizontal (X–Y) plane, making it particularly
       suitable for insertion and assembly tasks.





                                                                               3 | P a g e

       Industrial manipulators estimate tool position using forward kinematics based on
      sensed joint positions rather than direct tool sensing. Compliance causes sag under
       gravity or loading, producing positioning errors despite accurate joint sensing.


Q.9   The primary reason a SCARA robot is described as selectively compliant is that it is:

      (A) Flexible in the Z-direction and rigid in the X–Y plane

      (B) Rigid in the X–Y plane and compliant in all rotational axes

      (C) Rigid in the Z-direction while compliant in the X–Y plane

      (D) Equally compliant in all directions

       Explanation: (C) Refer Slide 4 of Lecture Manipulator Design Example

    A SCARA manipulator is designed to be rigid along the vertical (Z) axis while
       allowing limited compliance in the horizontal (X–Y) plane, making it particularly
       suitable for insertion and assembly tasks.





                                                                               3 | P a g e

Q.10  According to the Jacobian analysis on SCARA robot, singularity occurs when:

      (A) 𝜃₁ = 90°

      (B) 𝜃2 = 90°

      (C) 𝜃2 = 0°or 1800

      (D) 𝜃4 = 180°

       Explanation: (C) Refer Slide 14 of Lecture Manipulator Design Example

      The determinant of the Jacobian is proportional to 𝑙1𝑙2 sin 𝜃2. Hence singularities

concepts.title: Quintic endpoint constraints
concepts.description: The quintic requirement follows from six independent endpoint conditions, not from claiming that a lower-degree polynomial is internally nonsmooth.

concepts.title: Cubic rest-to-rest segment
concepts.description: A cubic can match endpoint positions and velocities; these four conditions do not also impose zero endpoint acceleration.

concepts.title: LSPB continuity qualification
concepts.description: Ordinary LSPB provides continuous velocity at the blend boundary but not continuous acceleration; the printed acceleration-continuity claim is not generally correct.

concepts.title: Qualified orientation travel
concepts.description: For the explicitly fixed axis, compare equivalent angle displacements modulo 360°. This does not justify subtracting arbitrary 3D rotation vectors as a universal orientation metric.

concepts.title: Repeatability versus accuracy
concepts.description: Repeatability concerns consistency across repetitions, whereas accuracy concerns closeness to the desired target.

concepts.title: Annular two-link workspace
concepts.description: The reachable radial interval is 1≤r≤9 m; maximum reach alone is not sufficient to establish reachability.

concepts.title: Redundancy and local self-motion
concepts.description: One local redundant direction is available; finite motions must still respect joint limits, collisions and changing singularities.

concepts.title: Compliance and rigid kinematics
concepts.description: Rigid forward kinematics can be inaccurate under compliance even when joint-angle measurements are accurate.
